text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Prime Minister Rafik Hariri will meet U.S. President Clinton on October 18 in Washington.
-Hariri to visit the Maronite patriarchate today to discuss the issue of the religious audiovisual media.
-Clashes between protesters and police during the second sit-in of the media workers protesting the government decision to slash the number of private television and radio stations.
-Lebanon received used 108 M113 armored personel carriers from the U.S. army.
-Banque Beyrouth pour le Commerce issues euro certificates of deposit for $12 million.
-The cabinet meeting on Wednesday did not discuss the media issue.

-Lebanese Assosiation for the Democracy of the Elections accuses the government of defaming democracy and confiscating the right of the Lebanese people to choose their representatives freely in the parliamentary elections.
-Lebanese University teachers staged a peaceful sit-in demanding giving some qualified teachers staff positions.
-Strong earthquake shakes Lebanon and East Mediterranean.
